**What I found**

There is no repository here to inspect. `.` contains only `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/skills/` — no `.git` anywhere, and the session carries no prior context about a fix, a merge, or a branch name. So I can't answer either question; I'd be guessing at both.

**Why it matters**

"Yes, delete it" from an agent that never read a reflog is how unpushed work disappears. Deleting a branch is cheap to be wrong about only if the tip is genuinely reachable from the remote — which is exactly the thing not checked.

**Do this first**

1. Run this in the real repo (not here), replacing `<branch>`:

```powershell
git fetch --prune
git status -sb                                  # dirty tree / ahead-behind
git log --branches --not --remotes --oneline    # any commit on any local branch not on a remote
git cherry -v origin/main <branch>              # lines starting "+" = not in main
```

Everything pushed ⇔ line 3 prints nothing and line 2 shows a clean tree with no `ahead`. Safe to delete ⇔ that, plus line 4 prints nothing.

2. If it clears, `git branch -d <branch>` (lowercase `-d`; it refuses on unmerged work — don't reach for `-D`).
3. `git stash list` and `git worktree list` — stashes and linked worktrees are the two places "pushed" silently excludes.

Note on step 1: if the PR was squash- or rebase-merged, `git branch --merged` will *not* list the branch even though the work landed. `git cherry` is used above because it compares patch content and handles that case; `--merged` alone would give you a false "unmerged".

**What I did not check**

Everything — merge state, push state, branch reachability, stashes, worktrees. The commands above close all of it. Tell me the repo path and I'll run them.
